newsitem.title: USA: Colo. disputes U S West rate request.
newsitem.headline: Colo. disputes U S West rate request.

text.p: The Colorado Public Utilities Commission said on Thursday its staff disputes U.S. West Inc's U S West Communications' request for a residential rate rise, saying that residential service is covering its full cost.
"The staff provides cost studies which show no increase is justified," the commission said in a statement.
"U S West's numbers don't add up to the company's proposed $3 monthly residential rate increase," said staff team leader Bruce Armstrong.
In May, U S West asked for permission to raise residential basic service rates by $3 a month to $17.95 and decrease business rates for basic service by $2 a month to $35.39.
The commission also said that residential rates may actually decrease if customers become eligible for $20 million in bill credits because of U S West's poor quality of service.

The Denver-based regional phone company, which provides service in a sprawling 14 state area in the West, has been at loggerheads with the commission over customer complaints about poor service. The phone company has blamed the problems on greater than expected growth and the need to place phone lines in remote areas. It has also said that service has been improving and good service remains a priority. The commission makes a decision on the rate request on January 27.
